title: The Broken Passage
premise: Juniper Okafor, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Voss Syndicate, takes a salvage contract to recover a vanished government survey team's equipment in the flooded delta country. Following a compass recovered from the site, Juniper discovers the team didn't vanish — they found an abandoned colonial-era passage beneath the river, and one survivor, cartographer Elias Wren, is still alive inside it, guarding a secret the government wants buried: a map of waterways that could redirect the monsoon floods and make someone very rich. Hunted by syndicate collectors, a corrupt survey official, and the rising waters themselves, Juniper and Elias must navigate the broken passage in a leaking boat before the monsoon seals it forever. In the end, Juniper chooses to release the map publicly rather than sell it, erasing their debt at the cost of everything else — and walks out of the flood with nothing but the compass and, for the first time, no one to owe.
about_author: Yara Underhill is a former river guide who spent six seasons on the delta waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people whose survival depends on reading weather, water, and other people correctly.

chapters.title: Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: Juniper Okafor's POV. We open mid-storm as Juniper chases a cell over the delta, chasing data they can barely afford to collect. Back in port, Voss Syndicate collector Marisol gives them seventy-two hours. The emotional beat is the claustrophobia of owing money to people who smile while they threaten you.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A fixer offers Juniper a salvage job: recover gear from a vanished government survey team upriver, paid enough to clear half the debt. Juniper inspects the offered boat — old, leaking, but seaworthy if babied. The beat is wary hope: a door opening that might also be a trap.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, first day upriver. Juniper reaches the survey camp: tents intact, instruments running, meals half-eaten, mud showing no footprints leaving. Only a brass compass sits centered on the chart table, pointing not north but downriver. The beat is dread dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Compass Lies South
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Testing the compass against their own instruments, Juniper confirms it points toward something submerged near a drowned church spire. They radio it in; the reply orders them to leave the compass and come back empty-handed. The beat is the first crack: someone doesn't want this found.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Elias Wren, alive and hiding in a flooded cavern system, hears a boat engine above. He has survived eleven days on ration bars and rainwater, keeping out of sight of the men who come looking. The beat is fear sharpened into patience.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the Water
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Juniper dives the spire, finds a breached stone archway, and surfaces inside the passage — face to face with a starving man holding a flare gun. Elias mistakes Juniper for one of 'them' until Juniper shows the syndicate debt notice instead of a badge. The beat is mutual suspicion becoming reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He explains: the team mapped a pre-colonial waterway network under the delta, and their lead, Director Hale, realized controlling the maps meant controlling the floods — and the land values after them. When two surveyors objected, Hale sealed them in. Elias escaped into the dark. The beat is horror delivered calmly by a man too tired to dramatize it.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They load Elias and the copied charts onto Juniper's boat just as the monsoon's first true band hits. The hull leak worsens; Juniper improvises patches while Elias bails. The beat is competence under pressure — the first time either trusts the other with their life.

chapters.title: Marisol Calls
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Via satellite phone, Marisol reveals the syndicate financed the survey through a shell company; the debt was always bait to put a deniable asset on the river. She offers to forgive everything if Juniper delivers Elias and the originals. The beat is betrayal reframing the whole journey: Juniper was the weapon all along.

chapters.title: Hale's Men
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A government patrol boat sweeps the channel, using sonar to search the passage entrances. Elias recognizes the search pattern as Hale's own protocol and realizes Hale isn't covering up a disappearance — he's hunting a witness. The beat is hunted-animal tension.

chapters.title: Into the Broken Passage
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. To evade both patrol and storm, Juniper takes the boat into the submerged passage itself, navigating by Elias's hand-drawn charts and the brass compass. Low ceilings, black water, one moment where the propeller fouls on old scaffolding. The beat is terror transmuted into focus.

chapters.title: The Drowned Church
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sheltering in a vaulted air pocket, Elias shows Juniper the full map — and admits he burned the originals' location into his memory only, because his partner Ada died protecting it. Juniper confesses they nearly sold him already. The beat is confession as intimacy; two compromised people choosing honesty.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The monsoon peaks; river levels climb, meaning the passage's air pockets will flood within days. The exit Elias used is now underwater. There is exactly one other way out, through a collapse zone Hale's survey flagged as unstable. The beat is the clock becoming audible.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Someone has been inside the passage recently: fresh rope, drained fuel drums, and a cut section of Juniper's mooring line. Hale's advance man, Okonjo, is already here, sealing exits to trap them. The beat is paranoia — the maze is being closed around them by human hands.

chapters.title: Okonjo
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Confrontation in a narrow gallery: Okonjo offers Juniper the same deal Marisol did, revealing the syndicate and Hale are partners, each planning to betray the other. Juniper stalls, then triggers a rockfall to escape, injuring Okonjo. The beat is moral cost — survival requiring a violence Juniper can't undo.

chapters.title: Ada's Route
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Grieving and resolute, Elias reconstructs his dead partner's alternate route from fragments she taught him verbally — a route she never wrote down because she didn't trust paper. It runs through the deepest, most flooded section. The beat is inheritance: carrying the dead forward by doing what they trained you for.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The transit: boat disassembled and portaged piece by piece through chest-deep water, oxygen thinning, Elias hypothermic, Juniper talking him through it with storm-chaser patter. The beat is endurance as devotion — the relationship's quiet climax before the plot's loud one.

chapters.title: Surface and Snare
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They surface into the storm's eye — deceptive calm — directly into a rendezvous between Hale's patrol boat and Marisol's collectors, each waiting to double-cross the other. Juniper and Elias are spotted immediately. The beat is the trap closing with the sky unnaturally still.

chapters.title: Everyone's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. On Hale's boat, the alliances detonate: Hale tries to arrest Marisol's crew, Marisol reveals recordings of Hale ordering the surveyors sealed in, and in the chaos Juniper gets Elias overboard with the charts hidden in a waterproof case. The beat is cathartic chaos — every corrupt actor consuming another.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Adrift in the eye's calm before the storm returns, Juniper holds the only complete copy of the map. Selling it clears the debt; releasing it publicly saves the delta villages but makes them enemies of everyone. Elias refuses to decide for them. The beat is the theme made concrete: power, or the price of refusing it.

chapters.title: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper broadcasts the map to every news outlet, hydrology office, and village council within signal range as the monsoon's final wall hits. They ride out the storm wrecked but alive on a shoal, Marisol's voice promising consequences over a dying radio. The beat is terrible freedom — the debt unpaid, the soul intact.

chapters.title: Nothing Owed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, weeks later. The map has stalled Hale's project pending inquiry; the delta towns are petitioning with it; Juniper is broke, semi-famous, and free. Elias leaves on a research vessel, pressing the brass compass into Juniper's hand. Final image: Juniper checks it — it points north now. The beat is quiet resolution: identity rebuilt around what you refuse to owe.
